title: What a dip is + Fear & Greed
bullets: 💧 A dip is a sharp drop in the price of something, like Bitcoin falling hard in a short time. That's what we were in on Nov 25.
🌡️ The Fear & Greed index scores crypto's mood from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed). On Nov 25 it was 13 (Extreme Fear).
🧠 It doesn't predict the future. It just shows whether the crowd is panicking or piling in.
📌 Fear can mean lower prices. It does not mean the bottom is in, or that buying is safe.

title: What Bitcoin is
bullets: 🪙 Bitcoin is digital money that no company or CEO runs.
🔢 Only 21 million will ever exist. That fixed supply is why people call it "digital gold."
🌐 Thousands of computers worldwide keep its record of who owns what.
📉 It's not a company stock: no earnings, no boss. Its price is just what buyers and sellers agree on, which is why moods like today's fear move it so much.

title: Wallets
bullets: 🔑 A crypto wallet doesn't hold coins. It holds the keys that prove the coins are yours.
🏦 If an app or exchange holds your keys, they control the coins. If you hold them (self-custody), you do.
📝 Self-custody wallets give you a seed phrase (12 or 24 words). That IS your money.
🚫 Never share it, type it into a website, or send it to "support." Anyone with those words can empty your wallet.

title: Exchanges
bullets: 🏪 An exchange (like a crypto app) is where you buy and sell coins with dollars.
🪪 You make an account and verify your ID first. That's called KYC.
🏦 Coins left on an exchange are held by them, like Lesson 3's custodial wallet. Moving them to your own wallet means you hold the keys.
🔐 If you keep coins on one, lock the account with 2FA. That's exactly what AI hackers look for.
